# QADREN

QADREN is a cross-platform file transfer and synchronization system. Rust owns cross-platform business logic. SwiftUI is the macOS control interface.

## Required reading

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `README.md`
3. `docs/README.md`
4. `docs/decisions/D-018-local-first-priorities.md`
5. `docs/architecture/backup-model.md`
6. `docs/architecture/technology-stack.md`
7. `docs/roadmap.md`
8. The matching policy, design, or development document for the change.

## Release 1

- Release 1 file operations use "This Mac" (Local Filesystem) and the "Сетевой диск (SMB)" connector (`smb_share`). An SMB share is mounted at `~/.qadren/mounts/<connection_id>` and uses the Local Filesystem executor. Core refuses SMB work unless that mount is present. See `docs/decisions/D-021-smb-network-drive-connector.md` and `docs/decisions/D-022-smb-in-release-1-scenarios.md`.
- Use one Rust JobStore. A `Scenario` defines synchronization rules. A `Job` is one execution or manual file operation.
- Keep each `StorageConnection` independent. Bind OAuth and Keychain state to `connection_id`.
- A one-way Scenario can use Yandex Disk (`yandex_disk`) as the source and a Local Filesystem or SMB root as the destination. The app runs these Jobs; the background Worker refuses them. Yandex Disk as a destination is stage 2. See `docs/decisions/D-023-yandex-disk-to-mac.md`.
- iCloud is post-release. Do not add iCloud work without a new owner decision.
- Do not add content versioning, runtime BackupSet, Scenario dependencies, or remote Worker protocol.

## Safety

- Do not save secrets in SQLite, Git, logs, or HTTP URLs.
- Remove and Disconnect change local state only. They do not delete provider objects.
- Read content needed by an enabled or requested operation without a separate prompt. Do not prefetch unrelated content.
- Before a modifying external effect, save a durable attempt. Check capability, exact scope, destination state, no-overwrite for new files, and required destructive consent.
- If effect proof is lost, reconcile without mutation. Persist a verified outcome only when evidence is sufficient. Otherwise retain `UNKNOWN`.
- A Local Filesystem update can replace an existing destination only through the approved replacement protocol.
- A Scenario revision has selected objects and a deletion mode: Paranoid (every deletion asks) or Simple synchronization (an approved rule, Trash first, 20-deletion threshold). See `docs/decisions/D-019-scenario-selection-and-deletion-modes.md`.

## Documentation

Repository documentation contains stable contracts. GitHub Issues contain active work, audits, current test results, and closure criteria. Git history contains change history.

Canonical documents:

- Product order: `docs/decisions/D-018-local-first-priorities.md`
- Architecture: `docs/architecture/`
- Safety: `docs/policies/`
- UI: `docs/design/`
- Build and release: `docs/development/build-and-release.md`
- Testing and quality: `docs/development/testing-and-quality.md`
- Product stages: `docs/roadmap.md`

Write changed project documentation and external tracker text in English and ASD-STE100 style. Use short active sentences and exact technical names. Do not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance without an approved-dictionary check.

## Verification

Record the SHA and worktree state before changes. Run checks relevant to the patch. `bash scripts/test-core.sh` is the standard Core check. On a supported Mac, run `bash scripts/build-macos.sh` and applicable native checks. Report only checks that ran. Mark unavailable checks as `BLOCKED` or `SKIPPED`.

Before commit, push, or PR, run the project-scoped AI Docs Hub pre-publish gate and repeat code and security review for the exact patch.
